title: Loops
description:
Write these with loops:

```rust
fn fizzbuzz(n: u32) -> Vec<String>          // "1", "2", "Fizz", ..., "FizzBuzz", up to n
fn collatz_steps(n: u64) -> u32             // steps for n to reach 1 (n / 2 when even, 3n + 1 when odd); 0 for n = 1
fn primes_below(n: u32) -> Vec<u32>         // in order; use a sieve
fn first_square_above(limit: u64) -> u64    // the smallest perfect square strictly greater than limit
```

Use `loop`, `while` and `for` where each fits best; `collatz_steps` can use `loop` with `break` returning the count.
hints: A `Vec` is a growable list (lesson 3.01 covers it fully): `let mut v = Vec::new();` makes an empty one, `v.push(x)` adds to the end, and `vec![false; n]` makes one holding `n` copies, like the array `[0; 5]`, indexed with `v[i]` (`i` a `usize`). `i.to_string()` turns a number into a `String`.
Matching on a tuple `(i % 3, i % 5)` handles the four FizzBuzz cases in one `match`.
A sieve keeps a `vec![false; n]` of "known composite" flags: each prime found marks its multiples, starting at its square.
